item.title: Reliable Computation of the $L_{\infty}$-Norm of Linear Time-Invariant Systems Depending on One Parameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.13048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $L_{\infty}$-norm of a linear time-invariant system is a central quantity in robust control, used in robust stability tests, stability margins, and $H_{\infty}$ controller design. Physical models depend on parameters, such as masses, stiffnesses, or gains, so the $L_{\infty}$-norm becomes a function of these parameters. This computation reduces to studying the real critical points of a plane algebraic curve whose coefficients depend on the parameters. Previous approaches based on cylindrical algebraic decomposition describe the $L_{\infty}$-norm on the whole parameter space, but their cost grows very quickly with the number of parameters. In this paper, we propose instead to compute a generic parametrisation of the solutions, valid outside an explicitly characterised set of non-generic parameter values. In the case of one parameter, this parametrisation is obtained by interpolation from a certified solver for the non-parametric case. The resulting algorithm is fully certified, relying on a priori bounds and multimodular computations rather than on Gr\"obner bases. It is illustrated on examples from the robust control literature.
item.dc:creator: Florent Corniquel (SU, UPCit{\'e}, IMJ-PRG), Alban Quadrat (SU, UPCit{\'e}, IMJ-PRG), Fabrice Rouillier (SU, UPCit{\'e}, IMJ-PRG), Grace Younes (SUAD)

item.title: 51 Additions per Recursive Step for Rank-23 $3\times3$ Matrix Multiplication, Machine-Checked over Arbitrary Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.12907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a rank-23 bilinear scheme for $3\times3$ matrix multiplication that uses 51 additions per recursive step in the alternative-basis (Karstadt-Schwartz) cost model, one below Nielsen's 52 (arXiv:2609.06588). The count 51 itself was first posted, on a different scheme, by Stapleton and Perminov (arXiv:2609.32388), found by heuristic sparse-basis search; the present work is independent and complementary: exactness and breadth rather than a single construction. The scheme is valid over every ring, so it recurses on block matrices, and its correctness is machine-checked in Lean 4/Mathlib. The count is exactly optimal for the scheme's equivalence class: we introduce an exact free-basis minimization procedure whose negative answers are exhaustion proofs, and use it to show that 51 is the minimum for this class, that 52 is exactly optimal both for Nielsen's class and for the class of the current flat-model record, and to sweep the complete Heule-Kauers-Seidl database of rank-23 classes. The sweep is complete: exactly four classes attain 51, all in a single HKS invariant family. We machine-check Stapleton and Perminov's scheme as well, and prove in Lean that their 51 is optimal for its class. Separately, we document a systematic gap between $\mathbb{F}_2$ and signed optima: the $\mathbb{F}_2$-optimal chains of a class typically admit no sign assignment under most of the class's integer sign models, and certificate lifting fails where a direct signed search succeeds.
item.dc:creator: Greg Sidebottom

item.title: Symmetric compatibility of theta structures, with applications to change of level and isogenies
item.description: arXiv:2504.21058v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $m,n,d >1$ be integers such that $n=md$ and let $(B, \mathscr{M}, \Theta\_{\mathscr{M}})$ be a marked abelian variety of level $m$ over a field of odd characteristic. We study the theta structures of level $n$ for $\mathscr{M}^d$, and the theta structures on the abelian varieties $d$-isogenous to $B$, which are compatible with $\Theta\_{\mathscr{M}}$. When $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, they correspond to the isotropic subgroups of $B[n]$, and this correspondence underlies the known algorithms in theta coordinates. In general, this is no longer true. We introduce the notion of symmetric compatibility of a torsion point with a symmetric level subgroup, and we show that a subgroup of $B[n]$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^g$ comes from a compatible theta structure if and only if it is isotropic and all its points are symmetric compatible. We extend to every $d$ Mumford's notion of compatible pairs of theta structures, defined by Mumford for $d=2$, and prove that it is equivalent to our notion, which can be tested on theta coordinates; we also describe exactly the remaining ambiguity, which explains the sign choices met when the duplication formula is used to change the level. As applications, we obtain change of level and isogeny algorithms without assuming that $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, using $O(n^{3g} \log(d))$ and $O(n^{2g} \log(d))$ operations in the base field respectively. In particular, they give change of level algorithms for even $d$, and $2$-isogenies in level $4$ theta coordinates with an explicit control of the theta structure of the codomain.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Dequay (IRMAR), David Lubicz (DGA.MI, IRMAR)

item.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
item.description: arXiv:2504.16771v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yirmeyahy Kaminski

item.title: An Effective Version of Kronecker's Theorem on the Splitting of Polynomials and the $p$-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2510.00892v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an effective version of Kronecker's Theorem on the splitting of polynomials, based on asymptotic arguments proposed by the Chudnovsky brothers, coming from Hermite-Pad\'e approximation. In conjunction with Honda's proof of the $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations with polynomial coefficients we use this to deduce an effective version of the Grothendieck $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations. More precisely, we bound the number of primes for which the $p$-curvature of a given differential equation has to vanish in terms of the height and the degree of the coefficients, in order to conclude it has a non-zero algebraic solution. Using this approach, we describe an algorithm that decides algebraicity of solutions of differential equation of order one using $p$-curvatures, and report on an implementation in SageMath.
item.dc:creator: Florian F\"urnsinn, Lucas Pannier

item.title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.05664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A neuro-symbolic system should combine only relevant answers from expert agents or other knowledge sources. Using only relevant experts for a given input query becomes ever more important for accuracy and scalability as the knowledge network grows and connects ever more knowledge sources. We extend the standard definition of relevance from the legal theory of evidence: An answer is relevant if and only if it is both probative and material for the matter at hand given the knowledge available. We apply this relevancy scheme to mixing the feedback fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) of real or artificial experts. The expert FCM directed causal graphs mix or combine into a common knowledge network. We compare the equilibrium limit-cycle predictions or answers of the experts to the answers of the mixture FCM and then estimate the probative status of answers by their difference or variation. A new Bayes-like theorem de-mixes the knowledge mixture into corresponding posterior-like FCMs that also allow relevancy-based comparisons. The result is a final set of relevancy mixing weights that produces a relevancy-mixed FCM knowledge network for the given query. So different queries produce different relevancy-mixed FCMs. We demonstrate this relevancy approach using generated synthetic FCMs from an actual 13-node expert FCM that models the causes and feedbacks of ischemic-stroke risk.
item.dc:creator: Olaoluwa Adigun, Akash Kumar Panda, Bart Kosko
